prerequisites: Preferable knowledge of the basic elements of statistics, the concept of random variable and the main discrete and continuous distributions.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of reliability theory in the broader context of quality, consistent with current regulatory definitions.
Basic concepts related to the study, measurement, evaluation, and interpretation of reliability performance of electrical/electronic equipment and ICT devices.
Operational tools to improve system reliability performance and for drafting reliability reports.
Methodological concepts for measuring and verifying product conformity to specified requirements and monitoring production process performance for improvement.
Necessary elements for undertaking product and system certification processes; knowledge elements of European Directives.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge on reliability models and corresponding statistical parameters (MTTF, MTBF, MTTR), on canonical functional configurations.
Ability to perform predictive reliability calculations and adequately select components based on the operating environment.
Ability to evaluate product conformity characteristics and production process characteristics.
Ability to intervene in correcting production processes to maximize their characteristics.
Ability to interpret norms, technical rules, and community directives for product and organization certification, as well as CE marking.
Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret information and data to make judgments on the reliability performance of a component or apparatus.
Ability to interpret information and data from a production process and make judgments on the quality level of production.
Ability to interpret a community directive, a standard or family of standards aimed at product and apparatus, organization and/or laboratory certification.
Ability to communicate acquired competencies to others; through laboratory experience, acquire communication skills to demonstrate in group work.
Acquire autonomy in selecting and interpreting technical documentation on the topics covered in the course.
Ability to evaluate reliability performance for a component/system.
Ability to calculate MTTF and MTBF values for an electronic apparatus.
Ability to perform failure rate evaluations and reliability predictions using databases.
Ability to appropriately select electronic components to optimize system MTBF and reliability/availability performance.
Ability to correct design based on improving reliability performance.
Ability to appropriately identify quality control methodologies.
Ability to apply and interpret some control charts for variables.
Ability to perform process capability analysis and calculate related indices.
Ability to evaluate the “quality” of a production process in terms of the percentage of conforming products.
Ability to identify problems related to certification activities.
Ability to appropriately select certification bodies and undertake the process for both product and system certification.

syllabus_topics: Methodologies for analyzing and evaluating the reliability of components and systems.
Techniques for calculating reliability in ICT.
Methods for predicting the failure rate.
Concepts of statistical quality control with monitoring and correction techniques.
Variability of production processes and measurement of product conformity.
CE marking, product and system certification.

Introduction to standardization, certification, and accreditation. Conformity, reliability, maintainability, availability (dependability), quality: temporal evolution of concepts and related definitions (UNI EN ISO 9000:2008, CEI 56-50 standards).
Failure, breakdown, and their classification. Reliability functions, experimental failure distribution, instantaneous failure rate, reliability and availability parameters: MTTF, MTBF, MTTR.
System reliability: series, parallel, stand-by, k-out-of-n, mixed configurations. Overview of complex configuration reliability.
Databases (MIL-HDBK 217 and others), failure rate calculation and reliability prediction for electronic equipment: part count and part stress methods.
Reliability analysis of complex systems: inductive and deductive methods, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and their Criticality Analysis (FMECA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA).
Techniques for increasing reliability/availability and reliability reports.
Quality control: product and process control, natural and specification tolerance.
In-line quality control, control charts (mean and range charts), Pareto diagram, cause-and-effect diagram.
Conformity measures. Statistical process control.
Analysis of random and systematic variability. Process capability analysis. Centered and non-centered processes. Capability and performance indices.
Normal distribution, mean and variance correction. Techniques for improving production processes.
New approach policy, European Directives, and concept of essential safety requirements.
Accreditation (ACCREDIA) and certification; product certification, quality marks, and CE marking; product certification process.
Overview of company quality system certification, process approach, and UNI EN ISO 9000:2008, Quality Manual, and system certification process.
Laboratory activities and exercises covering specific topics of the course.
assessment_rules: The final exam is an oral examination with a discussion of the laboratory report. The oral exam covers questions related to the three sections of the teaching program, equally weighted. The three parts (Reliability, Quality Control, Certification) have equal weight in terms of points, expressed out of thirty. Judgment autonomy and communication skills are verified through discussion, and learning ability is verified through the laboratory report.
